title: Giants trade reliever Ryan Walker to Brewers for 2 minor-league pitchers
content:
Perhaps no player in the San Francisco Giants organization needed a change of scenery more than struggling right-hander Ryan Walker. Perhaps no organization is better at pitching reclamation projects than the Milwaukee Brewers.

Now the Brewers have a new project. They seized a buy-low opportunity on a pitcher who was one of the National League’s better relievers two seasons ago, acquiring Walker from the Giants on Sunday for minor-league right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry.

Walker, 30, had a breakout season in 2024 when he went 10-4 with 10 saves and a 1.91 ERA in 76 appearances as a setup man for Camilo Doval. Leveraging an extreme, cross-firing delivery and a knee-buckling slider, Walker averaged 11.1 strikeouts and just 5.6 hits per nine innings.

But he followed up with pedestrian numbers in 2025 and couldn’t nail down the closer role after the Giants traded Doval to the New York Yankees. The Giants hoped that Walker could grab the ninth inning this past season, but his performance fell off a cliff. He posted a 7.16 ERA in 33 games, was hit hard and his walk rate soared. He had nearly as many walks (19) as strikeouts (23) in 32 2/3 innings — a stunning fall for a reliever whose 5.5 strikeout-to-walk ratio was among the game’s best in 2024.

Walker pitched his way so far out of the picture that the Giants, who were decimated by injuries and tied a major-league record by using 71 players, didn’t recall him in September.

Last week at the general managers’ meetings, Giants president Buster Posey told NBC Sports Bay Area that Walker’s career was “at a crossroads.”

“I’m a big fan of just Ryan Walker the person,” Posey said. “I think he would even say his confidence is a little rattled right now. He’s going to have to find a way to regain that confidence. Sometimes guys can go home in the offseason and they can put on a lot of really good muscle and weight and they come back and maybe their fastball is a little sharper and their breaking ball is a little sharper.

“He’s in that spot right now where he’s kind of at a crossroads and he’s going to have to decide which way his career is going to go. I’m more than hopeful that he can get it back going.”

So are the Brewers, who are hoping to augment an electric pitching staff that led the franchise to its first World Series championship. The Brewers already worked wonders for one former Giants pitcher, scooping up left-hander Kyle Harrison after the Giants had included him in the deal that netted Rafael Devers from the Boston Red Sox and getting an All-Star-adjacent first half from the 25-year-old as a member of their rotation.

Neither Holub nor Perry are among the Brewers’ top 10 prospects as ranked by Baseball America. Perry, 23, was Milwaukee’s 11th-round selection in the 2026 draft out of Western Kentucky University and hasn’t made his pro debut. Holub, 28, was a 15th-round pick of the Detroit Tigers out of St. Edward’s University (Texas) whom the Brewers acquired for first baseman Mark Canha after the 2023 season. Holub posted a 2.10 ERA in 50 relief appearances for Triple-A Nashville this past season.

Walker was one of three Giants pitchers, along with Landen Roupp and JT Brubaker, who were reprimanded by MLB after they wrote Bible verses on their hats that featured a rainbow logo when the Giants held their Pride Night on June 12. With Brubaker filing for free agency, Roupp is the only pitcher from that group who remains in the organization. Pitcher Sam Hentges, who is still with the team, declined to wear the hat with the rainbow logo.
